newsitem.title: FRANCE: Roussel sees 96 profit at 16 pct of sales.
newsitem.headline: Roussel sees 96 profit at 16 pct of sales.

text.p: French pharmaceuticals firm Roussel-Uclaf made operating profits of 17.5 percent of turnover in the third quarter and expects to make 16 percent at the end of the year, Roussel's finance director said on Wednesday.

Daniel Camus told a news conference to announce Hoechst's offer to buy out the shares outstanding in Roussel that Roussel aimed to hit 20 percent in 1998, which would be "an intermediate step" as the pharmaceutical industry average for profitability was 23 percent.
Hoechst's offer to buy out the 43.47 percent of Roussel prices the French firm at a P/E ratio of 26, he said.

That P/E ratio, which is based on a market consensus of 58.8 francs per share, is higher than the industry average of 23 for French pharmaceutical firms, he added. He did not specify the period to which he was referring.
